clue.text: Around Italian leader, non-functioning staff

parts.note: CA, short for circa, is Latin for around
Il Duce was the title of Mussolini, Italy's Fascist leader
US is slang for useless, i.e. not working

explanation.surface: A broken staff of office belonging to some Italian leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like workers next to 'non-functioning', but it is the definition: the herald's rod.
explanation.definitionFit: The caduceus is the winged rod carried by Hermes, a herald's wand.

clue.text: Inexperienced actor in the company is playing the goat …

indicators.note: in means the actor goes inside the company

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
a ham is an amateurish, overacting performer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A ham actor in the troupe is fooling about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing the goat' means fooling around, but here 'playing' is a link and 'the goat' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This agile mountain animal of the Alps is a goat-antelope.

clue.text: … to nonplus the silent cast

parts.note: dumb means unable or unwilling to speak
to found metal is to cast it in a mould

explanation.surface: To baffle the cast of a silent play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like actors, continuing from the previous clue, but means shaped in a mould.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish someone so they are lost for words is to baffle them.

clue.text: Very important, but not in the suburbs

explanation.surface: Something crucial that is not out in the suburbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Key or essential is one sense; located in the middle of town is the other.

clue.text: Savage is wild and mute

indicators.note: wild means the letters of and mute run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A savage creature is both feral and silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild, never domesticated or tamed, is the sense of savage here.

clue.text: Exactly what's needed for drying

explanation.surface: Something exact required to dry things off.
explanation.walkthrough: An actor who 'dries' forgets their lines, and needs a cue from the wings.
explanation.definitionFit: Punctual or exact timing is a sense of the adjective; in theatre a cue given to an actor who forgets lines is the noun.

clue.text: Write and order octets for the festival

parts.note: to pen is to write

indicators.note: order means the letters of octets are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Composing and arranging eight-part pieces for a church feast.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitsun, the Christian feast seven weeks after Easter, is a festival.

clue.text: Unmentionable haunts of school leaver?

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil of a school
one's scene is the places one frequents

explanation.surface: The dubious hangouts of a pupil who has just left school.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecent or offensive matter is too shocking to be spoken of.

clue.text: Get colleague to carry up cloak

parts.note: a pal is a mate or friend

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for carry is written upwards

parts.note: to tote is to carry

explanation.surface: Ask a workmate to lift a cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose overcoat of French origin, worn as an outer cloak.

clue.text: Regrouping, I mount main assault with plenty of this

indicators.note: regrouping means the letters of the words I mount main are reorganised

explanation.surface: A commander regroups to launch a main attack, well supplied with shells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regrouping' sounds military but asks for the letters of I MOUNT MAIN to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An attack is best mounted with plenty of bullets and shells, the supply a gun needs.

clue.text: Scotsman leaves wise guy alone

indicators.note: leaves means the word for a Scotsman departs from the wise man's name

parts.note: Solomon was the Biblical king famed for wisdom
MON is the Scots dialect form of man

explanation.surface: A Scot walks out on a smart alec, leaving him on his own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wise guy' suggests a smart alec but means King Solomon, famed for his wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: A performance or flight done unaccompanied is done by oneself.

clue.text: Turnover of shoes was high in the last century

definitions.text: Turnover of shoes was high in the last century

parts.words: Turnover of shoes was high in the last century
parts.note: a pair of brogue-style lace-ups being moved about, read also as a High Church revival of the nineteenth century

explanation.surface: Shoe sales were brisk in the previous century.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxfords are lace-up shoes; the High Church (Anglo-Catholic) revival based at Oxford University ran from the 1830s, the 'last century' when this puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tractarian revival led by Newman and Keble pushed Anglicanism towards High Church ritual in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Slovenly group of soldiers overwhelm the light infantry

indicators.note: overwhelm means the soldiers' group engulfs the light infantry, surrounding it

parts.note: a squad is a small unit of soldiers
LI is the abbreviation for Light Infantry

explanation.surface: An untidy squad of troops overruns a light infantry unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Squalid describes something dirty and neglected, which is close to sloppy and unkempt.

clue.text: He's taken .the cloth binding

explanation.surface: A man ordained and tied to his post.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish vicar or rector holds a church living; as an adjective the word means obligatory, as in a duty.

clue.text: Good man, clothed in sweetness and virtue

indicators.note: clothed in means the good man is wrapped inside the sweetness

parts.note: honey is the sweet substance bees make
ST, saint, is a good man in crosswords

explanation.surface: A saintly man dressed in sweetness and goodness.
explanation.definitionFit: Truthfulness and integrity are a classic moral virtue.

clue.text: Surfaces need a clean — that's a criticism, by the way.

parts.note: sides are the faces or surfaces of something
a wipe is a quick clean

explanation.surface: Remarking that the sides need cleaning is a dig.
explanation.definitionFit: A passing critical remark made incidentally is a dig.

clue.text: Spot a prelate inside the race enclosure

indicators.note: inside means a and the prelate go within the spot

parts.note: a pock is a spot or pustule on the skin
DD, Doctor of Divinity, stands for a senior churchman

explanation.surface: Spotting a bishop at the racecourse enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' looks like a verb (see), but it is a noun, a pockmark.
explanation.definitionFit: At a racecourse horses are paraded in a small fenced field before the race.

clue.text: Senior officer who, if white, would be a flier

definitions.text: who, if white, would be a flier

explanation.surface: A top officer who, if pale, could fly.
explanation.walkthrough: The white admiral is a British butterfly.
explanation.definitionFit: A top naval commander is one sense; the white admiral is a butterfly, a flying insect.

clue.text: One who leaves in the lurch a farm-worker

definitions.text: One who leaves in the lurch

explanation.surface: A labourer who abandons people.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abandons people is one sense; a labourer who digs drainage channels in fields is the other.

clue.text: Achieve great fame by organising smart do

indicators.note: organising means the letters of smart do are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Win celebrity by throwing a stylish party.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrity status, being a star, is the state of great fame.

clue.text: Principal combatants under the weather, as far as I can see

definitions.text: as far as I can see

indicators.note: under means in this down clue the combatants come below the weather

parts.note: the sky is where weather happens
the line is the front-line regiments of an army

explanation.surface: The chief fighters, unwell, see to the horizon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under the weather' suggests feeling ill, but here 'under' places LINE beneath SKY.
explanation.definitionFit: The horizon outline of land and buildings marks the limit of view.

clue.text: He does not 'believe in 'a West End robbery

indicators.note: End here means the final letter of the word West

parts.note: a heist is a robbery

explanation.surface: Someone sceptical that a robbery happened in London's theatre district.
explanation.walkthrough: The West End is London's theatre district, but 'West End' here gives the last letter of West.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rejects the existence of God, a non-believer.

clue.text: Building for two of the family line

parts.note: ma is a mother, one family member
a son is another family member
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A house built for two relatives of one lineage.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonework laid by builders, the craft of building in stone.

clue.text: Pythagoras's doctrine, when encountered, knocked me back to serious mental condition

parts.note: met is the past tense of encounter

indicators.note: knocked back means the word me is turned round
knocked back means the word me is turned round

parts.note: taken as written
psychosis is a severe mental disorder involving loss of contact with reality

explanation.surface: An ancient doctrine, once met, drives me to madness.
explanation.definitionFit: Transmigration of souls after death was a belief taught by Pythagoras.

clue.text: Support for the Chief

explanation.surface: Backing for the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved structure holds up a bridge or roof; as an adjective or prefix it means principal, as in archbishop.

clue.text: Cite, we hear, for scholastic award

explanation.surface: Quote something said aloud to win a school prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cite' sounds like sight, and a sight or show is one sense; the other is a scholarship awarded at some schools and universities.
explanation.definitionFit: A public show or spectacle is one sense; at British schools and colleges a scholarship grant is another.

clue.text: May it flourish, though lacking a bit of bloom

indicators.note: lacking means the Latin motto goes without the letter a

parts.note: floreat is Latin for may it flourish, common in school mottoes

explanation.surface: Wishing something thrives even though a piece of the flower is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: FLOREAT is the Latin wish found in mottoes such as Floreat Etona.
explanation.definitionFit: A small flower forming part of a larger head, as in broccoli or a daisy.

clue.text: The Left find the year disastrous — tough!

indicators.note: disastrous means the letters of the year are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: Left-wing politicians suffer a terrible year, and it is hard going.
explanation.definitionFit: Hide-like toughness, as of overcooked meat or weathered skin.
